Bioimage analysis · Advanced microscopy · Artificial intelligence

Seeing cells
in space and time.

I’m Cesar Valades-Cruz, an associate researcher at the Institute of Hydrobiology, Chinese Academy of Sciences. I develop microscopy and AI-assisted bioimage analysis methods to understand how cells organize, move, and divide.

Explore researchGet in touch

Research

From images to insight

My work connects optical imaging, computational methods, and cell biology across three complementary areas.

Full research overview ↗
01 / CURRENT FOCUS

Cyanobacterial cell division

Automated segmentation, tracking, and quantitative analysis of cells and filaments to study growth and differentiation.

Read more ↗
02 / IMAGING METHODS

Polarization & super-resolution

Measuring molecular orientation and nanoscale structure in actin networks and other biological assemblies.

Read more ↗
03 / COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS

3D live-cell image analysis

Restoration, tracking, visualization, and data workflows for complex microscopy datasets.

Read more ↗

At the Institute of Hydrobiology

Quantifying life, one cell at a time

My current research studies how cyanobacterial cells grow and divide. Image analysis lets us follow individual cells within filaments and connect their behavior to larger biological patterns.

About

Biology meets optics and computation.

My path has taken me from mechatronics in Mexico to biophotonics in France and Spain, then to cell imaging at Institut Curie and Inria. Today I work in Wuhan, China, with Prof. Cheng-Cai Zhang’s team.

I enjoy building tools that turn difficult microscopy data into useful biological measurements, and collaborating across disciplines to make those methods available to others.

Based inWuhan, China
Current roleAssociate Researcher · Institute of Hydrobiology, CAS
